explanation: When related entity types share some facts but also have subtype-specific facts, generalization is appropriate. Shared attributes belong in the broader entity, while attributes that apply only to one subtype stay in that subtype.

options.text: Keep the shared facts in a broader supertype and put salary and hourly rate in separate subtypes
Store salary and hourly rate in the same attribute because they both represent pay
Eliminate the shared name and email fields from the model
Force employees and contractors into one entity with no subtype distinctions

prompt: A company stores information about employees and contractors. Both have a name and a work email, but only employees have a salary and only contractors have an hourly rate. What is the best modeling approach?
